title: Tradition
description: Reference schema for docs/timeline/SPEC.md §7.1's Tradition node type — a religious/cosmological system modeled as a time-varying entity (implements P3: never a rung on a linear-progression ladder). Requires a TraditionDating object (§5.2, implements P8: oral traditions get the five/six-date treatment, never one fake-precise date) and non-hierarchical category_tags. Entities aggregate claims; they assert nothing on their own — every substantive statement about a Tradition lives in a linked Claim (subject_type: Tradition, subject_id: this entity's id), not inline here. The hand-rolled validator (docs/timeline/scripts/validate-timeline.mjs) is authoritative if this file and the validator diverge.

category_tags.description: SPEC.md §7.1 / P3: tags, never rungs on a ladder. A tradition may carry more than one tag (e.g. a tradition with both ancestor veneration and a high god carries both tags, not a forced single label).

dating.description: TraditionDating object, SPEC.md §5.2. Any of the six dated fields may be null; dating_summary is mandatory.

dating_summary.description: One honest sentence, e.g. 'Earliest securely documented practice c. X; earlier origins probable; how much earlier unknown.'

relationships.description: SPEC.md §7.2 edge types. An influence edge without a source that asserts the influence is invalid — motif similarity alone cannot create an edge.

target_id.description: Id of the entity (Tradition, Polity, etc.) at the other end of this edge.

claim_id.description: The Claim that sources this edge.
